item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Same Street After Dark

turns.text: Make this look like nighttime, not sunset. Keep the same street and the person where they are.

item.tests: Tests day-to-night relighting without replacing the scene or altering its subjects and layout.

answer_sheet.Nighttime look: Clearly after dark, not dusk or sunset. The exact lighting style is your call.
answer_sheet.What must stay?: The same shops, street, objects and pedestrian in their original positions.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Keep the original 16:9 framing; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Additional text or objects: No added text or new objects.

must_haves: The scene clearly reads as nighttime rather than sunny morning or sunset.
The street and shop architecture retain their original shapes and positions.
The pedestrian remains on the right in the same pose and blue jacket.
Nighttime illumination is coherent, with the original strong daylight appearance removed.
The original wide composition is preserved, with no new subjects or objects.

dialog.agent:
Yes, I can edit it. What would you like changed? Here are some ideas for this street scene:

- **Remove people:** take out the man in the blue jacket, the woman on the left, or both, so the street is empty.
- **Change the weather or time of day:** make it rainy, snowy, sunset or nighttime with the streetlights on.
- **Restyle it:** turn it into a watercolor, a vintage photo, an anime scene or a painting.
- **Change details:** repaint the shopfronts, add readable shop signs, or add bikes, café tables or more trees.
- **Add something:** put a person, car or object into the scene.
- **Remove the background:** cut out a subject.
- **Make it sharper:** upscale it to a higher resolution.

Tell me what you want, and I'll make the edit and send you the download link.
dialog.why: It asks the user what edit they want, offers options, and waits for their choice.
dialog.user: make it look like nighttime, not sunset. keep the same street and the person where they are

turns.agent:
I couldn't make the edit. Magic Hour refused it because your account doesn't have enough credits, so no image was created.

I tried the cheapest image-editing option your free plan allows, which costs about 5 credits. Every other editing model on the free plan costs more, so switching wouldn't help.

To go ahead, you'd need to add credits in your Magic Hour account, either by buying a credit pack or by waiting for your free credits to refill. Once you have credits, I'll run the same edit: a real night sky with no sunset glow, the streetlights on and the shop windows lit. The street and buildings will stay the same, and both people will stay where they are.
